name: The captivity of Israel (the northern kingdom)
charge: Two centuries of the sins of Jeroboam; secret sins; idols, high places, and children through the fire
summary: Second Kings 17 is the indictment of a nation: they feared other gods, walked in the statutes of the heathen and of the kings of Israel, built high places in every city, served idols the Lord had said they should not, made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil.
offense: Hoshea's conspiracy and withheld tribute occasioned Assyria's siege, but the account gives a deeper cause for Israel's removal: they sinned against the Lord who brought them out of Egypt and feared other gods (2 Kings 17:3-8). Political events carried a judgment rooted in the covenant they had forsaken. The Lord repeatedly sent prophets and seers to call them back to his statutes. They refused, hardened their necks, followed vanity, and continued the calves, Baal worship, divination, and the burning of their children (2 Kings 17:13-17). Repetition of warning was evidence of mercy; repetition of refusal made the guilt no less deliberate.
judgment: Samaria fell after a three-year siege. Israel was carried to Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes (2 Kings 17:5-6). The land from which their fathers had driven other worships no longer protected them while they practised those same departures. Assyria brought other peoples to dwell in the cities. Their mixture of reverence for the Lord and service to their own images did not fulfil the command to serve him alone (2 Kings 17:24-41). The account also warns that Judah had failed to keep the commandments (2 Kings 17:19). The northern kingdom's fall was not permission for the southern kingdom to presume upon its own continued place.

Assyria brought other peoples to dwell in the cities. Their mixture of reverence for the Lord and service to their own images did not fulfil the command to serve him alone (2 Kings 17:24-41). verses.text: For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,
And walked in the statutes of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which they had made.

And the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the Lord their God, and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.
And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree:
And there they burnt incense in all the high places, as did the heathen whom the Lord carried away before them; and wrought wicked things to provoke the Lord to anger:
For they served idols, whereof the Lord had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.

Yet the Lord testified against Israel, and against Judah, by all the prophets, and by all the seers, saying, Turn ye from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets.
Notwithstanding they would not hear, but hardened their necks, like to the neck of their fathers, that did not believe in the Lord their God.

And they rejected his statutes, and his covenant that he made with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testified against them; and they followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen that were round about them, concerning whom the Lord had charged them, that they should not do like them.
And they left all the commandments of the Lord their God, and made them molten images, even two calves, and made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.
Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.
For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin.
For the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did; they departed not from them;
Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.
Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.
By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.
Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus, saith the Lord, whose name is The God of hosts.
The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.

And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.
And I will scatter you among the heathen, and will draw out a sword after you: and your land shall be desolate, and your cities waste.

For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sins, till they were spoiled and carried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth: yet there remained a small people, and a ruler in the house of David:
Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.

entries.commentary: Hoshea son of Elah reigns nine years over Israel in Samaria and does evil, though not as the kings before him. Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up, and Hoshea becomes his servant and pays tribute. The king of Assyria finds conspiracy in Hoshea because he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped his yearly tribute, so he shuts him up in prison. Assyria besieges Samaria three years, then in the ninth year of Hoshea takes it and carries Israel away to Assyria, placing them in Halah, Habor, and the cities of the Medes.

This captivity comes because the children of Israel sinned against the Most High who brought them out of Egypt and feared other gods. They walked in the statutes of the heathen, built high places in all their cities, and set up images and groves on every high hill and under every green tree. They wrought wicked things to provoke the Most High and served idols, though He had said plainly, ye shall not do this thing. -

The Most High testified against Israel and Judah by all the prophets and seers, calling them to turn from evil and keep His commandments. They would not hear but hardened their necks like their fathers who did not believe in the Most High. To believe in the Most High is to take heed to the commandments, so those who claim belief while breaking the commandments do not truly believe. They rejected His statutes and covenant, followed vanity, made molten images and two calves, worshipped the host of heaven, and served Baal. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil. -

The Most High is very angry and removes Israel out of His sight, leaving only the tribe of Judah. Judah also fails to keep the commandments and walks in the statutes that Israel made. The Most High rejects all the seed of Israel, afflicts them, and delivers them into the hand of spoilers until He casts them out of His sight. This rejection is why the seed of Israel are later called heathens and Gentiles in the New Testament, which resolves much of the struggle over Jews and Gentiles there. -

The king of Assyria brings men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim to dwell in the cities of Samaria in Israel's place. Because they do not fear the Most High, He sends lions among them that slay some of them. One of the carried-away priests is brought back to Bethel to teach the settlers how they should fear the Most High.

Every nation makes gods of its own and sets them in the houses of the high places the Samaritans had made. The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, Cuth made Nergal, Hamath made Ashima, the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burnt their children to Adrammelech and Anammelech. They feared the Most High and also served their own gods after the manner of the nations they came from. The Most High made His covenant and charged the children of Jacob whom He named Israel, showing the covenant belongs to Israel and not to all nations.

The Most High commanded Israel not to fear, bow to, serve, or sacrifice to other gods, but to fear and worship Him alone who brought them out of Egypt with a stretched out arm. They were to observe His statutes, ordinances, and commandments forevermore, and He would deliver them out of the hand of all their enemies. No nation and no treaty can redeem Israel from their condition, only turning to the Most High can. These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations. -

Hear this word which the Lord takes up against the house of Israel, even a lamentation: the virgin of Israel is fallen, she shall no more rise, she is forsaken upon her land, and there is none to raise her up. The virgin of Israel is falling into all types of sin and sacrificing to other gods; we are supposed to be a chaste virgin, but the virgin of Israel played the harlot. -
Thus saith the Lord God: the city that went out by a thousand shall leave a hundred, and that which went forth by a hundred shall leave ten to the house of Israel.

Thus saith the Lord unto the house of Israel, seek ye me and ye shall live, but seek not Bethel, nor enter into Gilgal, and pass not to Beersheba, for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity and Bethel shall come to nought. Seek the Lord and ye shall live, lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph and devour it, and there be none to quench it in Bethel. If you worship these other gods and visit these other cities, the Lord will throw down everything.

Ye who turn judgment to wormwood and leave off righteousness in the earth, seek him that makes the seven stars and Orion, turns the shadow of death into the morning, makes the day dark with night, and calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth; the Lord is his name. He strengthens the spoiled against the strong, so that the spoiled shall come against the fortress.

They hate him that rebukes in the gate and abhor him that speaks uprightly, and they do the same thing today. Forasmuch as their treading is upon the poor and they take from him burdens of wheat, they have built houses of hewn stone but shall not dwell in them, and planted pleasant vineyards but shall not drink the wine of them. These curses are generational from each captivity, the same thing repeating over and over. -

For the Most High knows their manifold transgressions and mighty sins: they afflict the just, take a bribe, and turn aside the poor in the gate from their right, acting like they do not even see the poor, which is not the spirit of Christ. Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time. -

Seek good and not evil, that ye may live, and so the Lord the God of hosts shall be with you as ye have spoken. Hate the evil and love the good, and establish judgment in the gate; it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore the Lord the God of hosts says wailing shall be in all streets, they shall say in all the highways, alas, alas, and they shall call the husbandman to mourning and such as are skillful of lamentation to wailing. In all vineyards shall be wailing, for the Most High will pass through thee bringing judgment.

Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord; to what end is it for you? The day of the Lord is darkness and not light. This is a spirit checker; when you find yourself saying "I can't wait till Christ gets back," you had better examine yourself and get all the impurities out of you before that day, because you do not know what end it will be for you. It is as if a man fled from a lion and a bear met him, or went into the house, leaned his hand on the wall, and a serpent bit him. Shall not the day of the Lord be darkness and not light, even very dark with no brightness in it?

I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies. This is not talking about the feasts of the Lord, but about how Israel wanted to conduct the feast asking "is the Sabbath over yet," with no spirit whatsoever in it. Though ye offer burnt offerings and meat offerings, he will not accept them, nor regard the peace offerings of your fat beasts. Take away the noise of thy songs, for he will not hear the melody of thy viols; he does not want to hear anything, because we are not living according to the commandments.

But let judgment run down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream. Have ye offered unto me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, O house of Israel? But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god which ye made to yourselves. This was going on even during the time of Solomon. -

Therefore the Most High will cause them to go into captivity beyond Damascus, saith the Lord, whose name is the God of hosts. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe and to do all his commandments, the Most High will set thee on high above all nations of the earth. Diligent means characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort. You have to be on fire for the laws of the Most High, standing fast. You cannot be one foot in and one foot out, lukewarm, yawning through the classes. You cannot be tired of the word of the Lord; be excited to hear it.
All these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God. Hearken means to listen.

Blessed in the city and blessed in the field; blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, which is your children, and the fruit of thy ground and cattle. Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store: that is going into your surplus. Blessed when thou comest in and blessed when thou goest out: it is twofold, but it is going into coming in and out of Jerusalem.

The enemies that rise up against thee shall flee before thee seven ways; the blessing is commanded on thy storehouses and on all thou settest thine hand unto. The Most High shall establish thee an holy people unto himself, and all the people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord and be afraid of thee. Thou shalt lend unto many nations and not borrow; the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail, above only and not beneath, if thou hearken to the commandments and turn not aside after other gods. Isaiah sums up [Deuteronomy 28:1-14](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v1): we possessed it but a little while. Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships, and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings.

But if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee. Now we do some precepting, word by word. The voice of the Lord is his commandments; to hearken unto his voice means to keep his commandments. Observe to DO all his commandments: do is the action word. The Most High is a God of doing, and by him actions are weighed. Do not talk proudly and arrogantly, saying God loves me no matter what and God knows my heart; he had a personal relationship with a few men like Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, and David, and talking like you are one of them is arrogancy coming out of your mouth. Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

Cursed shalt thou be in the city: as when police fired on a car of siblings as young as nine years old in Georgia after the children panicked when a cruiser followed their vehicle. That is cursed in the city. Cursed shalt thou be in the field: we came off the slave ship and went right to the field, picking cotton from sunup to sundown. We know that one.

Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store: that goes into your businesses and your holdings. It is hard enough for a black man or woman to start a business; we are left with side hustles while the major trades, the ships, the metals, and the timber belong to Esau. These curses are on us as a nation. It is not about us individually; keep that in mind.

Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body: your children. The same children panicking in front of police, and the dozens of children killed by youth gun violence in Chicago in a matter of months. Cursed shall be the fruit of thy land, thy kine, and thy sheep: the food we eat is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us. Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as [Deuteronomy 14](/bible/deuteronomy/14) says.

Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in and cursed when thou goest out. He is talking about Jerusalem, but it is twofold: it is coming in and going out of life itself. Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: we are born under the curses and we die still living under them.

The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke in all that thou settest thine hand unto, until thou be destroyed. Rebuke means sharp disapproval or criticism because of your behavior: no matter what you do, nobody will see the silver lining in it; even what you mean for good turns out bad. Vexation means the state of being annoyed or a thing that causes annoyance: among these nations they do not love you, they tolerate you. Your marching for equal rights annoys them; they ask why you will not just accept what you were given.

The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee: diseases. He shall smite thee with a consumption, a fever, an inflammation, an extreme burning, the sword, blasting, and mildew. Amos shows what the blasting and mildew go into: famine, pestilence after the manner of Egypt, young men slain with the sword, death and destruction.

Thy heaven over thy head shall be brass, and the earth under thee iron. It is twofold: rain not coming down and crops not coming up. It also goes into the chains above your head and the shackles of iron on your feet. Look up the images of slavery and you see whose neck the chains were on. The rain of thy land shall be powder and dust from heaven until thou be destroyed.

Thou shalt go out one way against thine enemies and flee seven ways before them, and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth: 1492 and 1619. Thy carcase shall be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away. Look up Wounded Knee, where the United States cavalry killed the Native Americans, who are Gad in the Bible, and left their bodies in the snow.

The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, the emerods, the scab, and the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed. The itch that cannot be healed: look up who has the highest rates of sexually transmitted diseases right now. It is us.

The Lord shall smite thee with madness, blindness, and astonishment of heart, and thou shalt grope at noonday as the blind gropeth in darkness. Thou shalt not prosper in thy ways, and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee: going back into bondage. Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

Thou shalt betroth a wife and another man shall lie with her: our wives were taken away, raped, robbed, and murdered in the captivity. Thou shalt build an house and not dwell therein: we built the master's house, we built the White House, and to this day our people frame the roofs of suburban houses they will never live in. Thou shalt plant a vineyard and not gather the grapes: down south our people and the Haitians, who are Levi, are still in the fields picking beans and oranges, and none of it comes back to them; it is packaged and shipped somewhere else. Thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face and shall not be restored to thee: no reparations. They just pulled the okey-doke in North Carolina, promising reparations and then saying it would not be paid in money but in infrastructure. The Most High said it would not be restored.

Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look and fail with longing for them all the day long, and there shall be no might in thine hand. The slave narratives collected in When I Was a Slave back it up: slaves were treated like cattle, a speculator went about the country buying them up, and it was pitiful to see children taken from the mother's breast, mothers sold from children, husbands sold from wives. Another narrative: slavery days were hell; babies were snatched from their mother's breast and sold to speculators, children separated from sisters and brothers and never saw each other again. The Bible is a true book, and our ancestors backed it up.

The fruit of thy land and all thy labours shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up, and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway. The record of the conquistadors says one Spaniard ate enough for seven of the Indians, the northern kingdom. They literally ate up the fruit of the land. Thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.

The Lord shall bring thee and thy king unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone. Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations: Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, African American, gentile. We lost our name and left it for a curse, like it says in Isaiah, while others wear the name and cry anti-Semitic.

Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field and gather but little in; thou shalt plant vineyards but neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes; olive trees through all thy coasts, but no oil to anoint thyself. Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity: the same story the slave narratives tell. It happened before the ships too. When we ruled in Spain, in what they call the Dark Ages, a shipload of our people cast out on the African coast had the men and youths sold into slavery, the defenseless women ravished, and the aged, the sick, and the infants tortured and murdered by the thousands. That is recorded in The Jews and Moors in Spain; get that book if you do not have it.

All thy trees and the fruit of thy land shall the locust consume. The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high, and thou shalt come down very low; he shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him; he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail. Basically, you will always be oppressed. Their own book, New World Jewry, says the Jewish converts were so disseminated through all the trading parts of the world that they became the pegs and nails that keep the whole frame of commerce together, back in the 1600s. But the curse says Israel comes down very low and borrows from the stranger. The lender at the top of world trade and the cursed borrower cannot be the same people; somebody is lying, and now we caught it.

All these curses shall pursue thee and overtake thee till thou be destroyed, because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God. They shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. There is no time limit on this thing; that is how we know we are the real Israelites, because these curses are still hitting us all over the earth in some shape, form, or fashion to this day. The Most High said you would be the bottom, and he meant it until the kingdom comes. That is why they do not want to go to [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28).

Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart for the abundance of all things: we have to be happy keeping these commandments. That means joyful at the new moon, joyful on the sabbath, joyful in the classes. The lack of joy in keeping the commandments is the very reason the captivity came. Sisters, that includes the commandment to be obedient and in subjection to your husband. Do not act like it is bondage; your husband cannot save you on the day of judgment, and you must work out your own salvation and stand before Christ with a joyful spirit in the commandments.

Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in want of all things, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck until he have destroyed thee. Here is one way we stay destroyed: Juneteenth. The slave narrative records the master telling his slaves, this is military law, but I am forced to tell you this law says you are now free; I cannot make you stay unless you want to. That June 19th announcement of the master's law is what is still celebrated in Texas. Our people celebrate Juneteenth like it is something to be proud of, but it is the slave master's holiday, and we are still slaves under the curses.

The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth: the eagle is the symbol of Esau's nation. A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand: we did not speak English, and our brothers in the islands and South America did not speak Spanish when the ships came. New World Jewry itself records that many slaves were called ladino, which in that context means a negro slave who could speak Spanish. So the northern kingdom brother who says he is not black is simply a negro that speaks Spanish; welcome home, you are our brother. A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old nor shew favour to the young: they worked the old to death in the cotton fields, and today an old man dies with a knee held on his neck for over eight minutes, and children get fired on by police. Neither old nor young is spared.

He shall eat the fruit of thy cattle and the fruit of thy land until thou be destroyed, leaving thee neither corn, wine, nor oil. The Native Americans lived off the land, following the buffalo and the deer and making coats of skins. Now Reuben stays by the casino and Gad lives on reservation lands like barren wasteland where nothing grows, with outdoor plumbing, and it has never been restored. Reparations is not a casino, and it is not being called sovereign while occupied by another nation.

He shall besiege thee in all thy gates until thy high and fenced walls come down. Verse 52 onward is going into the siege of Jerusalem by Babylon and by Rome, and Assyria did this also. This is NOT talking about black-on-black violence; do not use it for that. Thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and daughters, in the siege and in the straitness wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee. The Most High starved our people out in the siege until they boiled and ate their own children. The proof it is not street violence is in the text itself: the tender man's eye shall be evil toward the wife of his bosom and toward the remnant of his children, because he has nothing left in the siege. It describes a good, caring, delicate man broken by famine, not violence in the neighborhood. The tender and delicate woman, which would not set the sole of her foot upon the ground for delicateness: our sisters have fallen a long way from that standard of tenderness and delicateness, and they need to return to it.

If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law written in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD THY GOD, then he will make thy plagues wonderful, plagues of thy seed, of long continuance, and sore sicknesses. Verse 59 is saying the Most High will make up diseases to keep punishing you; he will even have Esau create them in a laboratory and make them affect you more than anybody else. He will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt which thou wast afraid of, and also every sickness and every plague which is NOT written in the book of this law, until thou be destroyed.

Ye shall be left few in number, whereas ye were as the stars of heaven for multitude, because thou wouldest not obey the voice of the Lord thy God. As the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you. We have to understand who we are dealing with: he is happy to bless you and happy to destroy you for breaking the commandments. That is the God this Christianity needs to be teaching, to put some fear back in our people.

The Lord shall scatter thee among all people from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone: that is talking about Christianity and Islam. The Handbook of Denominations records that as early as 1700 white slaveholders in the south provided religious teaching for their slaves, and the slaves identified with the faith of their owners: if your slave master was Baptist you were Baptist; if he was Catholic you were Catholic. The same book says black Baptist doctrine runs quite parallel to that of white Baptist churches: it is the same exact thing, the slave master's religion with a black face on it. The Most High is saying: wherever I scatter you, you will not know me; you will be caught up thinking you serve me, but you do not know me. The only time you will know him is when he puts his spirit back on the earth and reveals it in the last days. That is why there is so much turmoil in our life, because we were not serving God right.

Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest, but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind. No ease: the northern kingdom is catching it right now, with migrant children taken from their families and detained in hotels not even registered with the government before deportation, and thousands of those children cannot be found.

Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee, and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life. That is why those children panicked when the police car pulled up behind them: no assurance of thy life. In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even, and at even, Would God it were morning, for the fear of thine heart and the sight of thine eyes.

Here is the nail in the coffin: the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships. Egypt means bondage; the scripture defines it right in [Deuteronomy 5](/bible/deuteronomy/5), the land of Egypt, the house of bondage. He is saying: I will bring you into slavery again, with ships. It is not the literal land of Egypt, because you can walk to Egypt; Isaiah shows Israel walked down to Egypt. The false pastors who say we were shipped back across the Red Sea are wrong; the ships went to a spiritual Egypt. Revelation names it: the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt. The greatest country on the face of the earth, America, Babylon the great, is the Egypt we were carried into with ships. Even their own scholarship confirms who was there the first time: a treatise on physical geography admits that negroes existed in Egypt in the days of Rameses with the same national features they have now. The Bible says the negroes go INTO Egypt, bondage, AGAIN. There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.
Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee; the quick precept for no man shall buy you.

The children of Israel are to make no idols nor graven images, rear up no standing image, and set up no image of stone in the land to bow down to it. That covers the images bowed to today: the cobblestone of Islam, the cross, and the relics and Egyptian heads that egyptologists worship. The Israelites are not to do that.

Keep the sabbaths of the Most High and reverence His sanctuary. When you came into the sanctuary you had better come with respect, because the Most High was putting men to death over it. Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, offered strange fire before the Lord which He commanded them not, and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them; that is what reverencing the sanctuary means.

These are the blessings for walking in the statutes and keeping the commandments, the same blessings and curses read in Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: rain in due season, the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought.

The threshing is the corn and the vintage is the grapes for the wine. The threshing reaching to the vintage and the vintage to the sowing time means one season's plenty would carry into the next. Israel would never be without wine, without crops, without food; each harvest would reach to the next season, and the bread would be eaten to the full in safety.

The Most High would give peace in the land: no enemies able to come against Israel, no war in the land, no one making the people afraid. That was fulfilled in the days of king Solomon, when there was rest on every side. That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid.

Israel would chase their enemies, and the enemies would fall before them by the sword; the nations feared Israel when the nation kept this covenant, as the book of Joshua shows. Five would chase an hundred, and an hundred put ten thousand to flight: that is how much power the Most High was going to bestow on His people, having respect unto them, making them fruitful, and establishing His covenant with them and their children.

Eating the old store and bringing forth the old because of the new means the storehouses would be so full that the old crop would have to be carried out to make room for the new; that is how plenteous the land would be. The Most High would set His tabernacle among the people, walk among them, and be their God; He brought them out of Egypt so they should not be bondmen, and broke the bands of their yoke.

This is the flip side. If Israel would not hearken but despised the statutes and broke the covenant, the Most High would walk contrary to the people, standing in exact opposition so that nothing would prosper. Terror is the terrorism lived under every single day: terrorized by wicked corrupt officers, by our own brothers and sisters, by the nations. Consumption is being consumed in the land, with diseases, oppression, financial mishaps, and the prison system; the burning ague goes into disease, harm to the eyes, and sorrow of heart in the mind. Sowing seed in vain: vineyards planted that the enemies eat, and children sown in vain, born only to be killed, incarcerated, or raised up under the curse.

The Most High set His face against Israel, and the people are slain before their enemies; you see that every single day. They that hate you shall reign over you: that is the clear explanation of why no laws will be passed to deliver this people and why there will be no reparations. No political party, Democratic or Republican, will be beneficial, because the curse stands and they that hate us now reign over us; and we flee when none pursueth.

Seven times more punishment for the sins, and the pride of Israel's power broken: the very power promised in the blessings, when enemies would flee, was taken away. That is the explanation of how the slave masters could bring Israel into slavery: they are not bigger or stronger nations, but it was divine intervention; the Most High broke our power and took our strength so the enemies could prevail. We outnumbered them many times in the cotton fields, yet could do nothing. The heaven as iron and the earth as brass also goes into the shackles on the neck and on the feet; and the strength is spent in vain, for the land yields no increase.

Walking contrary still brings seven times more plagues according to the sins. Wild beasts sent among the people to rob them of their children, destroy their cattle, and make them few in number: wolves, coyotes, bears, whatever the Most High would allow to come upon the people for their wickedness. That is real evil brought for real rebellion. It also goes into the pestilences and diseases loosed among the people in these last days, as [Revelation 6](/bible/revelation/6) bears out with death by sword, hunger, and the beasts of the earth.

If the people would not be reformed by these things, the Most High would punish yet seven times more and bring a sword to avenge the quarrel of His covenant; gathered into their cities, the pestilence would be sent among them and they would be delivered into the hand of the enemy. Breaking the staff of bread, with ten women baking bread in one oven and delivering bread again by weight, is straight poverty: a lack of resources and food. Many of us grew up literally knocking on the neighbor's door to borrow sugar, borrow the iron, borrow bread, use the grill at such and such house because our appliances did not work; that is this verse, the same thing to this day, eating and not being satisfied.

The Most High said He would walk contrary in fury, and He would be the one doing it: He would use the enemies, but it would be Him behind it. That is heavy. Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD, and it also happened in the days of the kings when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman's son was boiled and eaten.

The high places destroyed, the images cut down, and the carcasses of the people cast upon the carcasses of their idols: our people dying in the christian church with a cross around the neck, our people dying up against the cobblestone, still worshipping while they die. Even the high places themselves fall in judgment, as when a storm brought a church down on the congregation in Africa during a so-called easter program; that is what this verse reads about.

The Most High made the cities waste and brought the sanctuaries to desolation, and would not smell the savour of the sweet odours: He was not accepting the sacrifices, and He used the enemy to destroy the sanctuary. The Babylonians destroyed the temple, then the Greeks, then the Romans. When Babylon came against Jerusalem, Esau stood on the side cheering it on to the foundation, as [Psalms 137](/bible/psalms/137) records. Scattered among the heathen with a sword drawn out after them: not only the scattering, but death and anguish sent among the people in the lands of the captivity.

Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths as long as it lieth desolate. The land was to rest every seventh year, and the sabbaths were not kept: no cooking or tilling on the sabbath, the land resting every seven years, none of it. The Most High said the land could not rest while the people dwelt on it doing evil, so He rid the people out of the land so that the land could enjoy her sabbaths while it lay desolate without them.

Upon them that are left alive a faintness is sent into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that the sound of a shaken leaf chases them; the same trembling heart, failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind that [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) describes for the land of the enemies. Falling one upon another as it were before a sword when none pursueth: even at these protests, when the rubber bullets, the tear gas, the water hoses, and the dogs come out, the people stumble and fall over one another trying to get away. Still to this day the same thing. And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression.

They that are left pine away in their iniquity in the enemies' land, and in the iniquities of their fathers. You see people just decay in their sickness: the Most High may not judge a man right away but gives him space to repent, yet he keeps eating the defiled food, smoking his weed, doping, in and out of jail, and slowly pines away. It is a miserable life to live; we have to get right with the Most High.

Confessing the iniquity of the fathers and their own trespass, with the uncircumcised heart humbled, is exactly what is being done right now: repenting, confessing the sins, remembering that the sins of the forefathers are ours, and turning the uncircumcised mind back to the Father. Accepting the punishment of the iniquity means going through the trials without fighting the sentence: not marching for reparations or so-called equality, but accepting the punishment for the iniquities committed against the Most High.

When the people repent and turn back, the Most High remembers His covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, the covenant passed down to their children, the children of Israel; and He remembers the land. The land enjoys her sabbaths while she lieth desolate without them, and the people must accept that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes.

Yet for all that, in the land of their enemies the Most High will not cast the people away, neither abhor them to destroy them utterly and break His covenant. He sent Israel into captivity not for all to die, but to be afflicted until they finally turn back to the Lord God of Israel. So when you hear people say the Israelites are done away, that is a lie: the Most High promised He would not destroy the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but would give them a chance to repent and would remember the covenant of their ancestors whom He brought out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen. It also carries into the future tense.

These are the statutes and judgments and laws which the Most High made between Him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses. The quick recap of the chapter: these are the blessings and the curses that come upon the children of Israel for obedience or disobedience, and the chapter runs parallel with Deuteronomy the 28th chapter.

text.text: For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,
And walked in the statutes of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which they had made.

And the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the Lord their God, and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.
And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree:
And there they burnt incense in all the high places, as did the heathen whom the Lord carried away before them; and wrought wicked things to provoke the Lord to anger:
For they served idols, whereof the Lord had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.

Yet the Lord testified against Israel, and against Judah, by all the prophets, and by all the seers, saying, Turn ye from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets.
Notwithstanding they would not hear, but hardened their necks, like to the neck of their fathers, that did not believe in the Lord their God.

And they rejected his statutes, and his covenant that he made with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testified against them; and they followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen that were round about them, concerning whom the Lord had charged them, that they should not do like them.
And they left all the commandments of the Lord their God, and made them molten images, even two calves, and made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.
Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.
For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin.
For the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did; they departed not from them;
Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.
Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.
By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.
Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus, saith the Lord, whose name is The God of hosts.
The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.

And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.
And I will scatter you among the heathen, and will draw out a sword after you: and your land shall be desolate, and your cities waste.

For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sins, till they were spoiled and carried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth: yet there remained a small people, and a ruler in the house of David:
Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.
